business_problem: Michelin needed to replace a costly, slow SaaS master-data management system that delayed new features, slowed incident resolution, and made its global supply-chain product repository hard to evolve.
solution_summary: Michelin re-platformed its PS9 supply-chain master-data management application onto MongoDB Atlas to regain control over the product and services repository used by more than 60 internal applications. The team adopted a document-driven model so it could move faster than the old SaaS environment, where feature changes could take up to two years and even small incidents could take more than 20 days to fix. MongoDB’s native Kafka connector lets Michelin stream logistics and product events in real time, including data tied to 67 factories and warehouses in 171 countries, while Atlas collections give users a simpler way to manage evolving records. The migration was executed on a 10-month deadline, with data transferred between environments in hours, and Atlas now underpins a responsive platform for custom collections, faster calculations, and immediate issue analysis without shadow IT workarounds.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores Michelin’s PS9 product and service repository and provides the managed document database for the redesigned supply-chain application.

solution_components.name: Kafka
solution_components.role: Streams logistics and repository events into the new MongoDB-based architecture in real time.

data_flow: Supply-chain and product repository data are moved into MongoDB Atlas, Kafka feeds real-time logistics events from factories and warehouses, and PS9 collections serve operational updates, issue analysis, and downstream application queries across the business.
business_outcome: Michelin cut core PS9 processing from hours to seconds, reduced feature delivery from years to days, improved incident response, lowered costs, and created a more scalable data foundation for future AI work.
metrics: PS9 powers Michelin’s central Products and Services Repository, used by over 60 applications across the organization.
